name: Christian Menefee
bio: Christian Menefee has represented Texas's 18th district in the U.S. House since February 2026 and sits on the Oversight and Science, Space, and Technology committees. He was previously Harris County Attorney from 2021 to 2026, the youngest person and first Black attorney elected to that office, after working in commercial litigation. He grew up in Houston and is a graduate of UT San Antonio and Washington University School of Law.

platform.point: Pass Medicare for All, expand Medicare and Medicaid coverage to include dental, vision and hearing.
Make billionaires and large corporations pay more in taxes, expand family tax credits and help first-time homebuyers.
Ban assault weapons and bump stocks, close background check loopholes and limit high-capacity magazines.
Restore abortion rights in federal law, protect contraception and IVF, and block a national abortion ban.
Fully fund public schools, raise teacher pay, expand Pell Grants and create universal pre-K.
Seeks investigations of ICE shootings, body cameras for agents, and protection for DACA and TPS holders.

economy.evidence: Campaign calls for higher taxes on billionaires and large corporations and a higher minimum wage.

welfare.evidence: Campaign pledges to pass Medicare for All and free public and community college.

liberty.evidence: Supports federal abortion rights and LGBTQ protections (individual choice) but an assault weapons ban and magazine limits on guns.

security.evidence: Backs criminal justice reform, ending for-profit prisons and body cameras for ICE agents.

immigration.evidence: Defends DACA and TPS holders, seeks detention facility closures and ICE accountability.

energy.evidence: Campaign pledges tougher environmental protections and to defend Inflation Reduction Act climate progress.

tech.evidence: Calls for clear rules for AI and blockchain that protect consumers and workers.

education.evidence: Pledges to fully fund public schools and oppose dismantling the Department of Education.

notes: Liberty score of 30 is new and averages his abortion and LGBTQ positions with his support for gun restrictions. No official portrait flag in input; Commons file is a public-domain House portrait.

name: Ronald Whitfield
bio: Ronald Whitfield is a landscaping contractor and the Republican nominee for Texas's 18th congressional district. He also ran for the seat in the 2025–26 special election.
notes: No campaign website or public issue positions were found; Ballotpedia was unreachable during research.

name: Tom Sell
bio: Tom Sell is a Lubbock businessman and fifth-generation West Texan running for the open 19th district seat. He is a Texas Tech University graduate and previously worked for former U.S. Representative Larry Combest while Combest chaired the House Agriculture Committee.

platform.point: Supports strong border security and immigration control policies.
Promotes American energy dominance.
Pledges to champion agriculture and rural communities of the southern High Plains.
Supports a strong national defense.
Lists protecting the Second Amendment and protecting life as priorities.
Lists stopping Sharia law among his campaign issues.

liberty.evidence: Lists protecting life (abortion) and protecting the Second Amendment (guns) as priorities.

immigration.evidence: Lists strong border and immigration control policies as a top issue.

foreign.evidence: Lists a strong national defense among his priorities.

energy.evidence: Campaign pledges to promote energy dominance.

notes: The campaign issues page lists headings without detailed explanations, so scores rest on brief statements.

name: Kyle Rable
current_role: Texas Tech PhD candidate and U.S. Army Reserve captain
bio: Kyle Rable is a PhD candidate at Texas Tech University and a captain in the U.S. Army Reserve. He is a former secretary of the Lubbock County Democratic Party and a member of CWA Local 6186, and lives in Lubbock.

platform.point: Pass fair pricing legislation and limit large corporations from buying single-family homes.
Push federal AI and data center regulation, and restrict companies from selling personal data.
Freeze interest rates on loans to small family farms and expand sustainable farming support.
Cap prices on life-saving medicines such as insulin and fully fund rural hospitals.
Streamline and expand legal immigration pathways and keep protecting refugees.
Break up large monopolies and strengthen Small Business Administration support for family businesses.

economy.evidence: Proposes fair pricing laws, drug price caps, limits on corporate home buying and breaking up monopolies.

welfare.evidence: Calls healthcare a human right and pledges to protect Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security from cuts.

immigration.evidence: Wants to expand and simplify legal pathways to citizenship and continue accepting refugees.

foreign.evidence: Would co-sponsor repeal of presidential war powers to prevent more Middle East wars.

tech.evidence: Calls for federal AI and data center regulation, tougher data-privacy penalties and limits on selling personal data.

name: Joaquin Castro
bio: Joaquin Castro has represented Texas's 20th district, based in San Antonio, in the U.S. House since 2013, and serves on the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees. He previously served in the Texas House of Representatives from 2003 to 2013 and chaired the Congressional Hispanic Caucus from 2019 to 2021. He is a San Antonio native and a graduate of Stanford University and Harvard Law School.

platform.point: Seeks to close the Dilley family detention facility.
Urges San Antonio-area cities to end 287(g) immigration enforcement agreements with ICE.
Supports military aid for Ukraine but opposed a 2026 sanctions bill over tariff powers given to the president.
Pressing for transparency on a Venezuelan oil fund, including a push to subpoena the administration.
Reintroduced a bill to widen access to advanced coursework for underrepresented students.

economy.evidence: Record supports raising the minimum wage and keeping the estate tax.

welfare.evidence: Record opposes adding work requirements to welfare programs.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and same-sex marriage.

security.evidence: Urges local cities to end 287(g) agreements that let police enforce immigration law.

immigration.evidence: Supports DREAMers, pushes to close the Dilley detention center, and led the 2019 resolution against the border wall emergency.

foreign.evidence: Says he has consistently voted for military aid to Ukraine against Russia.

energy.evidence: Record includes support for the Green New Deal.

education.evidence: Record includes opposition to school vouchers.

notes: Foreign score raised from 50 to 65 based on his stated consistent votes for Ukraine military aid. OnTheIssues was unavailable during this pass, so scores sourced there are carried over from earlier research.

name: Edgardo Baez
bio: Edgardo Báez is an attorney running as the Republican nominee in Texas's 20th district. His campaign describes a background as a soldier and critical care nurse and more than two decades practicing law, and says his views were shaped by government overreach in Cuba.

platform.point: Stimulate local businesses and job creation and pursue tax reform.
Back law enforcement and defend critical infrastructure; endorsed by the San Antonio Police Officers Association.
Defend constitutional rights and oppose socialist policies.
Bring Christian principles and support for faith and family into legislation.

economy.evidence: Campaign pledges tax reform and job growth and opposes socialist policies.

security.evidence: Campaign pledges strong support for law enforcement and safer streets.

faith.evidence: Campaign says strong communities start with Christian principles paired with legislation.

notes: The campaign site uses the name Edgardo Rafael Báez. The site gives general themes rather than detailed policy positions.

name: Mark Teixeira
bio: Mark Teixeira is a former Major League Baseball first baseman who played 14 seasons for teams including the Texas Rangers and New York Yankees, winning the 2009 World Series. Born in Annapolis, Maryland, and a Georgia Tech alumnus, he moved to Texas in 2021 and worked with the Texas Public Policy Foundation on education issues. He won the 2026 Republican primary for the open 21st district seat.

platform.point: Fully secure the southern border, deport people here illegally and dismantle cartels.
Expand DOGE-style efforts to cut wasteful federal spending and bureaucracy.
Develop Texas oil, natural gas and nuclear power for energy independence and lower bills.
Protect parental rights, end DEI programs and remove progressive ideology from schools.
End prolonged military engagements and put American interests first.
Establish congressional term limits.

economy.evidence: Proposes expanding DOGE spending cuts and shrinking federal bureaucracy.

welfare.evidence: Wants lower healthcare costs through more patient choice and less federal involvement.

liberty.evidence: Pledges to protect the unborn (abortion) and to defend gun rights (guns).

security.evidence: Backs law enforcement and strict accountability for criminals.

immigration.evidence: Calls for securing the border and deporting people in the country illegally.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending prolonged military engagements abroad.

energy.evidence: Supports expanding Texas oil, gas and nuclear production.

education.evidence: Emphasizes parental authority and has worked with TPPF on educational freedom.

name: Kristin Hook
current_role: Scientist and former federal science policy advisor
bio: Kristin Hook is a scientist with a PhD in animal behavior from Cornell University who grew up in South Texas and studied at the University of Texas at Austin. She taught middle school science through Teach For America and later worked on science and technology policy in the office of Sen. Elizabeth Warren, at the National Institutes of Health and at the Government Accountability Office. She was the Democratic nominee for this district in 2024.

platform.point: Supports Medicare for All and opposes cuts to health insurance subsidies.
Centers her economic agenda on working families facing high costs and criticizes billionaires and CEOs.
Lists restoring abortion rights among her main issues.
Prioritizes investment in public schools.
Calls for accountability in government and the private sector, including big tech.
Seeks stronger voting rights protections.

economy.evidence: Frames her agenda around working families and criticizes billionaires and CEOs.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: her issues page calls for restoring abortion freedoms.

tech.evidence: Calls for accountability for big tech and the private sector.

education.evidence: Issues page prioritizes investing in public schools.

notes: Welfare score raised from 65 to 90 based on her support for Medicare for All. Her issues page shows only headings, so the immigration score was removed and the economy and liberty scores rest on brief statements.

name: Trever Nehls
current_role: Retired Army Reserve colonel and former Fort Bend County constable
bio: Trever Nehls served as the elected Constable for Fort Bend County Precinct 4 from 2013 to 2020 and founded Nehls Consulting. He is a retired U.S. Army Reserve colonel with more than 33 years of service, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan. He is the twin brother of retiring Rep. Troy Nehls, whose seat he is seeking.

platform.point: Finish the border wall, end catch-and-release and deport people who violate immigration law.
Lower costs through lower taxes, fewer regulations and a pro-growth agenda.
Defend parental rights, end DEI mandates and require curriculum transparency.
Expand oil, gas and nuclear production and cut energy regulations.
Fully fund and support law enforcement.
Finish SH-99 and support flood mitigation and mobility projects in the district.

economy.evidence: Supports lower taxes, fewer regulations and a pro-growth agenda.

liberty.evidence: Would block gender ideology in schools and protect girls' sports (LGBTQ); also backs gun rights.

security.evidence: Pledges to fully fund and support law enforcement.

immigration.evidence: Supports finishing the wall and deporting people in the country illegally.

energy.evidence: Supports expanded domestic oil and gas production and fewer energy regulations.

education.evidence: Emphasizes parental rights and parental choice in education.

name: Marquette Greene-Scott
bio: Marquette Greene-Scott is a city council member and mayor pro tem in Iowa Colony, Texas, and a former teacher who moved to Texas from Louisiana in 2010. She was the Democratic nominee for this district in 2024.

platform.point: Pass universal healthcare and protect the Affordable Care Act.
Fund the VA fully, strengthen oversight and expand mental health support for military families.
Pair more border security resources and faster case processing with a path to citizenship for people brought as children.
Protect voting rights, end partisan gerrymandering and tighten campaign finance rules.
Restore abortion rights after the overturning of Roe v. Wade.

welfare.evidence: Calls for universal healthcare not tied to employment.

liberty.evidence: Supports restoring abortion rights after Roe v. Wade was overturned.

immigration.evidence: Supports a path to citizenship alongside increased border security resources.

notes: Liberty score reflects only her abortion position, as other liberty issues were not found.

name: Brandon Herrera
bio: Brandon Herrera is an entrepreneur who founded a firearm manufacturing business and built a large YouTube following focused on firearms and Second Amendment advocacy. He moved his businesses back to Texas in 2020 and narrowly lost the 2024 Republican primary runoff for this district to Rep. Tony Gonzales before winning the 2026 nomination.

platform.point: Fund border technology and Border Patrol, and bring back the Remain in Mexico policy.
Signed the No New Taxes pledge and would sponsor the REINS Act to review major regulations.
Push national concealed carry reciprocity and block red flag laws and new firearm restrictions.
Sponsor legislation letting education funding follow students to public, private or parochial schools.
Bring troops home from Syria and Iraq and oppose large spending on foreign borders.
Co-sponsor a constitutional amendment limiting House members to three terms.

economy.evidence: Took the No New Taxes pledge and wants to roll back federal regulations.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion funding (abortion) but opposes red flag laws and new gun restrictions (guns); backs women's sports limits (LGBTQ).

immigration.evidence: Wants to reinstate Remain in Mexico and end asylum abuse, but says a wall is unnecessary in Big Bend.

foreign.evidence: Opposes sending billions to defend foreign borders and wants troops out of Syria and Iraq.

education.evidence: Would sponsor legislation for education dollars to follow students, and defends homeschooling.

name: Katy Padilla Stout
bio: Katy Padilla Stout is an attorney practicing child welfare and education law at her family's firm in Carrizo Springs and a former elementary school teacher in Northside ISD. A San Antonio native, she graduated from the University of Texas at Austin and South Texas College of Law, and has served on the Bexar County Child Welfare Board since 2017.

platform.point: Expand Medicare to all Americans, or strengthen the ACA, and grow community health centers.
Fund universal pre-K, raise the minimum wage and require paid parental leave.
Oppose the planned border wall through the Big Bend region.
Oppose tax cuts for billionaires and reshape the tax code toward the middle class.
Rejoin the Paris climate agreement.
Support universal background checks, a bump stock ban and red flag laws.

economy.evidence: Opposes billionaire tax cuts and backs a higher minimum wage and paid parental leave mandate.

welfare.evidence: Supports expanding Medicare to cover all Americans and universal pre-K.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights (abortion) alongside universal background checks and red flag laws (guns).

immigration.evidence: Supports reasonable pathways to citizenship alongside border security.

energy.evidence: Calls for rejoining the Paris Climate Accord.

education.evidence: Supports a major federal investment in universal pre-K.

notes: Commons photo is a CC0 own-work upload by a Wikimedia user.
